subject: DPA clarifications and breach notification flow for PilotEval
body_preview: Quick recap from our discovery: controller/processor roles, subprocessors, residency, retention and breach notification timing — please review attached redlines and confirm next steps.
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.infer>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@medpilot.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.infer>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.infer>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA clarifications and breach notification flow for PilotEval

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete asks so Legal/Tech can triage: 

Summary of our understanding from the demo/discovery:
- MedPilot will act as Controller for patient scheduling data; Redwood will be Processor for inference and logging.
- Pilot scope: anonymized scheduling + optional PII fields (name, email) for appointment reminders.
- Residency requirement: US-only for PHI-related items (customer requirement).

Open asks / next steps:
1) Please confirm "Controller vs Processor" language is acceptable — in particular we need explicit customer control over data residency and the right to delete records on request.
2) Subprocessor list: please share any vendor restrictions (e.g., no GCP in EU). We will attach our current subprocessor list, but want to see if you need to restrict to specific regions or providers.
3) Breach notification timing: you mentioned a 48-hour preference during the call — what is your minimum acceptable window? Our standard is: initial acknowledgement within 24 hours, substantial update within 72 hours.
4) Retention & logs: please confirm required retention for event logs and raw request traces (default Redwood logs 90 days; we can extend to 12/24 months for contractual reasons). Also indicate if you need schema/PII redaction examples.
5) DPA redlines: if you have redlines, send them back and we can route to Legal for a quick review.

Attachments: I attached an event-log-schema.csv for your tech review.

Proposed next steps: you share your redlines and SOC2 (or equivalent); we schedule a 30-min legal sync for Apr 11 to close outstanding items.

Thanks — I can pull in Solutions Engineering if you want a deeper dive on the dataflow.

—
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.infer
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@medpilot.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.infer>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.infer>
Cc: LegalOps <legal@medpilot.io>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications and breach notification flow for PilotEval

Evelyn — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from MedPilot/GTM & Legal: 

- Controller/Processor: MedPilot will be Controller. We expect Redwood to be Processor. Please ensure DPA language reflects that.
- Subprocessors: our security policy prefers to avoid non-US data residency for PHI. Can Redwood provide a list of subprocessors and confirm whether we can limit to US-only (for the pilot)?
- Breach window: Legal prefers notification within 48 hours of detection for incidents impacting PHI, but we understand operational realities. If Redwood can commit to an initial acknowledgement within 24 hours and a more detailed update within 48 hours for PHI incidents, that would be acceptable to us.
- Retention: for the pilot we require event/log retention of 12 months for traceability; can Redwood support configurable retention per customer?

I attached a redlined DPA (MedPilot_DPA_Redlines_v2.pdf) — mostly clarifications and a few suggested edits around notification timelines and subprocessor notice. Please confirm receipt and next steps for DocuSign.

Samir
Director, Partnerships — MedPilot Health
samir.khan@medpilot.io
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.infer>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@medpilot.io>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.infer>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.infer>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications and breach notification flow for PilotEval

Samir / Evelyn — looping in technical context to address the items Samir highlighted. Short answers below plus attachments with details.

1) Controller/Processor: Confirmed — Redwood takes Processor role in the DPA for the inference/serving path. We will ensure the DPA language maps to that (we can mark specific service boundaries in an appendix).

2) Subprocessors & residency: Current subprocessors include (operational partners): AWS (us-west-2), FastCache Inc. (managed caching), and LogStreamer LLC (ingestion pipeline). I'm attaching redwood-subprocessor-list-2028.csv with versions. For the PilotEval we can scope processing to US regions only and disable cross-region replication. We cannot guarantee absolute exclusion of certain underlying providers in all edge cases (e.g., emergency failover), but we can commit contractual language restricting processing to US-only for PHI and provide prior notice before adding any non-US subprocessors.

3) Breach notice timeline: Our standard operating practice is:
   - Detection & initial triage: immediate; customer-facing acknowledgement within 24 hours.
   - Material impact/phases: initial substantive update within 48–72 hours depending on investigation depth.
   - Final root cause & remediation report: delivered within 30 days by default, expedited if customer requests SLA exception.
For PHI-specific incidents we can commit to the 48-hour substantive update you requested (noted in redlines) while keeping the 24-hour ack. We'll mark that in the proposed DPA clause.

4) Retention & logs: Default audit/event logs: 90 days. We can configure 12 months for PilotEval as a contractual add-on. Raw request data containing PII can be set to 30/90/365-day buckets per customer. Event-log-schema.csv attached shows fields we capture and redaction options (we redact tokens and full-text by default unless explicitly allowed).

5) Evidence: we can provide our SOC 2 Type II report and recent penetration test summary under an NDA.

Next steps: 
- I will upload an updated DPA incorporating the 48-hour PHI substantive update and US-only processing clause, then route to Legal for quick review.
- Evelyn — can you send Samir a DocuSign link for the DPA once Legal signs off on the minor edits?

Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-list-2028.csv; event-log-schema.csv

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Technical PM, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.infer>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.infer>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.infer>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2028 11:00:00 -0700

Karthik / Priyom — thanks for the update. Quick internal notes before I send the DocuSign: 

- Legal confirmed they can accept the 48-hour substantive update commitment for PHI incidents; we will keep the 24-hour acknowledgement requirement.
- Priyom: please prepare the US-only processing clause language and escalate to Legal if it needs additional wording.
- I scheduled the legal sync for Apr 11 at 11am PT (calendar invite to Samir & LegalOps).

Forwarding the latest from Samir + Karthik below for context.

Evelyn

Redwood Inference
